slides.title: 4 words every first-time bidder should know
slides.sub: Bank-owned auctions have their own language. Here it is in plain English.

slides.pos: noun, short for real estate owned
definitions: A home a bank or lender took back after it didn't sell at foreclosure.
Often listed below market value, because the bank wants it sold.
slides.example: “It's an REO, so the seller is a bank, not a family.”

definitions: The lowest opening offer the auction will take.
Bids climb from here, one increment at a time.
slides.example: “The starting bid was $25,000, under half the estimate.”

definitions: The smallest amount each new bid must beat the last one by.
If the increment is $1,000, a $25,000 bid can only be topped by $26,000 or more.
Someone still lives in the home.
You usually can't tour inside before the auction, so the photos, reports and estimate matter more.
